blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Covers freedom fighters and political leaders who contributed to Gujarat's statehood and national independence.
Explores major scientists and scholars originating from or based in Gujarat.
Examines influential spiritual and religious leaders shaping social reforms in Gujarat.
Highlights prominent sports personalities representing Gujarat at national and international levels.

cells: Father of the Nation; led India's independence through non-violence; Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad
Iron Man of India; first Home Minister; integrated 562 princely states into India
Father of India's space program; founded ISRO; National Physical Laboratory
Wife of Mahatma Gandhi; participated in freedom struggle
Elder brother of Sardar Patel; First Indian President of Central Legislative Assembly
Led Mahagujarat Movement; founded Kisan Majoor Party
First Chief Minister of Gujarat; doctor and politician
Politician, writer, historian; founder of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan; started Somnath temple restoration
Prime Minister of India (1977–79); first non-Congress PM; Bharat Ratna
Social reformer; worked for untouchables and tribal upliftment

items: Vikram Sarabhai: Founder of ISRO and Physical Research Laboratory (PRL). Born in Ahmedabad. The Satish Dhawan Space Centre was formerly known as ISRO launch site.
Homi Bhabha: Though not from Gujarat, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre is linked to Gujarat's nuclear program at Kakrapar and Tarapur (though in Maharashtra).
Hemachandra (1088–1173 CE): Jain polymath; wrote grammar, poetry, history, philosophy. Advisor to Solanki king Kumarpal.
Dr. H.M. Patel: ICS officer and politician from Gujarat; Finance Minister of India.
Narsinh Mehta (1414–1481): First major poet of Gujarati literature. Composed 'Vaishnav Jan To' — Gandhi's favorite bhajan. Born in Talaja, Bhavnagar.

Swami Sahajanand (Sahajananda Swami / Lord Swaminarayan): Born in UP but founded the Swaminarayan sect in Gujarat; lived and preached in Gujarat; transformed Gujarati society. The Swaminarayan Sampraday is headquartered at Ahmedabad and Vadtal.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj: Fifth spiritual successor of Lord Swaminarayan (BAPS); built Akshardham temples.
Morari Bapu: Born in Mahuva (Bhavnagar); renowned for Ram Katha narrations worldwide.
Dada Bhagwan (A.M. Patel): Founder of Akram Vignan movement; born in Tarasali, Surat district.
Exams frequently ask about the key movements led by freedom fighters from Gujarat during the Indian independence struggle.
Focus on major institutions founded by scientists from Gujarat and their core scientific achievements.
Remember key spiritual reform movements and famous literary scholars originating from Gujarat.
Ranjitsinhji (K.S. Ranjitsinhji): Prince of Nawanagar; pioneered the leg glance in cricket; played for England cricket team; first Indian to play for England.
Duleep Singh: Ranjitsinhji's nephew; Duleep Trophy named after him.
Rohinton Baria: Pioneering cricket administrator from Gujarat.
Parthiv Patel: Gujarati cricketer; played for India as wicketkeeper.
Jasprit Bumrah: Born in Ahmedabad; star fast bowler for India; ICC Test Player of the Year 2023.
Hardik Pandya: All-rounder; born in Surat; IPL and Indian team regular.
